Baur JA.lab_name: Institute for Diabetes, Obesity, and Metabolism and Department of Physiology, Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA)
Baur JA.role: Senior (last) author of the 2012 Science study on rapamycin, insulin resistance and mTORC2 in mice.
Baur JA.sub: Institute for Diabetes, Obesity, and Metabolism · Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, USA
story: Joseph A Baur is last author of an Atlas study (LAM2012) on a puzzle about rapamycin. The drug extends lifespan in mice, yet long-term treatment makes them glucose intolerant and insulin resistant. The authors showed in mice that chronic rapamycin also disrupts a second complex, mTORC2, and that this loss explains the insulin problem. They also found that mice with less mTORC1 activity could live longer with normal glucose handling, so the two effects can be separated.

PubMed's record of this study lists no affiliation for Baur. The match to the University of Pennsylvania comes from a later paper by the same group (PMID 32268298), which shares four authors with this study and lists Joseph A Baur at the Institute for Diabetes, Obesity, and Metabolism there.

highlights.LAM2012: Last author: senior author of the mouse work showing that rapamycin disrupts mTORC2 and causes insulin resistance.

Jørgensen JO.lab_name: Department of Endocrinology and Internal Medicine, Aarhus University Hospital (Aarhus, Denmark)
Jørgensen JO.role: Senior (last) author of a 2013 randomised, placebo-controlled trial of high-dose resveratrol in obese men.
Jørgensen JO.sub: Department of Endocrinology and Internal Medicine · Aarhus University Hospital, Aarhus, Denmark
story: Jens Otto L Jørgensen is last author of an Atlas study (POU2013) in people. Twenty-four obese men took high-dose resveratrol or a placebo for four weeks. Resveratrol did not change insulin sensitivity, blood pressure or body composition, which goes against the promising results seen in rodents.

PubMed gives an affiliation only for the first author of this study. The Aarhus University Hospital link comes from a related 2014 paper by the same group (PMID 25050904), which shares five authors with this study and lists Jens O L Jørgensen in the same hospital department.

highlights.POU2013: Last author: senior author of the human trial that found no effect of high-dose resveratrol in obese men.

Parmigiani A.lab_name: Department of Human and Molecular Genetics, Goodwin Research Laboratories, Massey Cancer Center, Virginia Commonwealth University (Richmond, Virginia, USA)
Parmigiani A.role: First author of the 2014 cell study showing that Sestrins inhibit mTORC1 through the GATOR2 complex.
Parmigiani A.sub: Department of Human and Molecular Genetics · Massey Cancer Center, Virginia Commonwealth University, Richmond, USA
story: Anita Parmigiani is first author of an Atlas study (PAR2014) done in cells. It found that Sestrins, proteins made under stress, switch off mTORC1 by binding the GATOR2 complex. This keeps mTOR away from the lysosome, where it is normally activated.

PubMed has no affiliation for any author of this study. The Virginia Commonwealth University link comes from a related 2015 paper (PMID 26313705) that shares two authors with it, Boxiao Ding and Andrei V Budanov, and lists Anita Parmigiani in the same department.

highlights.PAR2014: First author: led the cell experiments showing Sestrins act on mTORC1 through GATOR2.
